problem: Find the general solution to the differential equation $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\sqrt{1-{y}^{2}}\,$ for $\,|y|<1.$

examples.knowledge_point: Finding a General Solution in Implicit Form
examples.worked_solution:
To find the general solution, we first separate the variables: 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{x}{y} \\ y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =x\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate both sides with respect to $x{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int y\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x & =\int x\,\text{d}x \\ \int y\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\cancel{\text{d}x}}\,\cancel{\text{d}x} & =\int x\,\text{d}x \\ \int y\,\text{d}y & =\int x\,\text{d}x \\ \frac{{y}^{2}}{2} & =\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+K \\ {y}^{2} & ={x}^{2}+2K \\ {y}^{2} & ={x}^{2}+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C= 2K.$

Therefore, the general solution to the differential equation (in implicit form) is

$$
y^2 = x^2 + C .
$$

feedback.problem:
Separate the variables in the following differential equation: 

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\sqrt{1+{y}^{2}}}{x}
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
A differentiable equation is *separable* if it can be written in the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=h(x)g(y).
$$

If an equation is separable, we say that the variables are *separated* when it is written in the form

$$
\frac{1}{g(y)}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=h(x).
$$

Notice that our differentiable equation is separable since it can be written as

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x}\cdot \sqrt{1+{y}^{2}}.
$$

Therefore, we separate the variables as follows:

$$
\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+{y}^{2}}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x}
$$
